title: Ukraine is arming war robots with grenade launchers to hit the Russians so its soldiers don't have to get too close
content:
Ukraine is mounting grenade launchers on ground robots, allowing its forces to bring useful firepower closer to Russian troops without sending in soldiers to pull the trigger.
Grenades have long been important in Ukraine's fight against Russia's invasion, particularly in close-quarters trench combat, but the battlefield is changing.
Troops increasingly fight in smaller force concentrations from scattered defensive positions rather than heavily manned continuous trench networks. Meanwhile, the growing "kill zone, which is swarming with drones, makes it harder for troops to approach these front-line positions. While infantry remains critically important, drones and robots are bridging the gap and taking over more and more missions, from logistics to medevac to assault.
Defense manufacturers told Business Insider that grenade launchers are increasingly being mounted on uncrewed ground vehicles, or UGVs, allowing soldiers to strike Russian positions from a safer distance.
Oleg Fedoryshyn, the director of R&D for the Ukrainian robotic and defense company DevDroid, told Business Insider that grenade launchers are useful because soldiers "don't need to see the enemy to hit him."
A soldier in hiding is easier to hit with a grenade launcher than, say, a machine gun, which is a line-of-sight weapon.
Now, soldiers can mount them on ground robots so that they don't have to put themselves in harm's way. A soldier-carried grenade launcher might have a range of a few hundred meters, but using a robot, an operator can be tens of kilometers away.
DevDroid's TW-40 ground robotic system has a range of 70 kilometers on paved roads and up to 50 kilometers off-road, making it effective in the kill zone. And the mounted grenade launcher has a reach of 1.5 kilometers.
Ukraine has been using soldier-carried and truck-mounted grenade launchers since before Russia began its full-scale invasion in February 2022. The robots deliver similar firepower without risking human lives.
Ukraine's Third Army Corps, for example, said in September that it used grenade launchers on robots to "dismantle enemy positions" in its Operation Vivaldi, characterizing it as "a new tactic."
"Equipped with dual Bullspike grenade launchers, the UGVs attacked Russian positions before detonating directly inside the enemy's shelters. The occupiers believed they were under assault by an entire assault squad; in reality, they were being pulverized by the Third Assault Brigade's robots," the brigade wrote on Telegram.
It said that robots were able to strike, put psychological pressure on Russian forces, and clear the position "all without putting our infantry at risk."
"This is a tactic never before seen in the history of warfare. The robots were controlled by operators from a secure shelter located tens of kilometers away from the front line."
Robots armed with grenade launchers are another example of how this war is blending elements of old warfare with new, advanced technologies. In this war, it's not uncommon to see drones dropping grenades or electronic warfare sharing the battlefield with artillery.
In addition to grenade launchers, robots can also fire other weapons, such as RPGs and American-made M2 Browning machine guns.
DevDroid's goal with its systems is "to change all roles that we can change to save people's lives," Fedoryshyn said.
That goal is shared by Ukraine's soldiers, defense industry, and leadership. Oleksandr Yabchanka, the head of the robotic systems for Ukraine's Da Vinci Wolves Battalion, told Business Insider that Ukraine is constantly working to increase the distance between troops and the fighting.
"Our philosophy is, above all, to preserve our personnel," he explained. "We strive to position our fighters as far as possible from the line of contact and the zones of highest risk — the so-called 'kill zones.'"
Other manufacturers say they're seeing a shift in how soldiers use armed robots in combat.
Defense firm Frontline Robotics makes the Buria autonomous remote weapon station, which allows soldiers to fire grenade launchers and other weapons remotely. Early last year, Ukrainian forces were hiding them in prepared locations to stop Russian advances.
"But right now, everything has changed," Mykyta Rozhkov, chief business development officer, told Business Insider, pointing to the growing drone saturation on the battlefield.
Now, it's being mounted on UGVs, creating small tanks that can advance toward Russian positions without exposing troops.
DevDroid's Fedoryshyn said robots armed with grenade launchers are most effective when paired with robots carrying machine guns and aerial drones that can spot targets and direct fire.
Robots can be used to transport gear, evacuate the wounded, blow up enemy positions, lay mines, and fire various types of weaponry. Their use has increased dramatically. Ukraine's defense ministry said in June that it had contracted over 22,000 uncrewed ground vehicles so far in 2026, nearly twice as many as all of the previous year.
The Da Vinci Wolves' Yabchanka said that he sees that "many units have begun employing UGVs. This usage has already become widespread. Ground-based robotic systems are becoming an integral part of combat operations for most units deployed along the line of contact."
As UGV use grows, Rozhkov said that Frontline Robotics' goal is to "provide different robotic solutions to get people outside the danger zone. So just to keep the line with the robots."

report.summary: 乌克兰在地面机器人上加装榴弹发射器，让士兵远离前线
report.background: 俄乌战场正从密集战壕对峙转向小规模分散据点，但无人机大量使用，使前沿形成难以接近的“杀伤区”，步兵接近阵地风险极高。乌方因此把榴弹发射器这类曲射、无需直视目标的武器搬到无人地面车辆（UGV）上：操作员可在数十公里外遥控射击，既保留火力又避免人员暴露。此前这类武器多由士兵携带或装在卡车上，如今平台化、遥控化正成为新趋势。乌克兰国防部称，2026年上半年已采购超过2.2万台UGV，接近去年全年的两倍。
key_points: 榴弹发射器属于曲射武器，不必看到敌人也能命中掩体后的目标，比机枪更适合由机器人携带，用来打击躲藏的俄军。
DevDroid的TW-40地面机器人公路续航70公里、越野50公里，搭载的榴弹发射器射程1.5公里，操作员可待在几十公里外的安全位置。
乌克兰第三军团称，在“维瓦尔第行动”中用双联装榴弹发射器机器人攻击俄军阵地，并直接突入掩体自爆，俄方一度误以为遭到整支突击队进攻。
战场无人机密度上升，使固定部署的遥控武器站改为装在UGV上，变成可前推的“小型坦克”；机器人最有效的用法是与机枪机器人、侦察无人机协同。
乌军把“最大限度拉开人员与接触线距离”当作原则，UGV已承担运输、撤离伤员、布雷、爆破和火力打击等多种任务，成为多数前线部队的常规装备。
report.impact: 对AI与机器人行业而言，这是无人地面平台从侦察、后勤走向直接火力投送的标志性案例，会推动遥控武器站、集群协同、抗干扰通信和低成本自主导航的研发与采购。对开发者来说，需求集中在远距离低延迟链路、目标识别与火控、多机协同，以及“人在回路”的可靠性与安全设计；这些会带来工程与伦理两方面的挑战。对普通用户而言，战争正在进一步无人化，平民与操作员之间的责任边界、自主武器的国际规制讨论将更受关注。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：ROS 2 + Nav2（导航与多机协同）、PX4/ArduPilot（无人平台飞控与地面车控制）、NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Gazebo（仿真训练）、YOLO 系列 + OpenCV/TensorRT（目标识别与边缘推理）、MAVLink 与自组网 Mesh 电台（远距低延迟遥测）。
